coachingPoints: The pack line is non-negotiable — one defender outside it breaks the whole defense
On-ball pressure must be real; sagging without ball pressure gives up rhythm threes
Closeouts from the pack must be under control — you are closing a longer distance
The pack only works if all five rebound — long shots mean long rebounds
Adjust the pack against elite shooting teams; the line can move out
commonMistakes: Defenders drifting outside the pack line to 'their man' — the gaps disappear
No ball pressure — the offense gets comfortable and picks the pack apart
Closing out wildly from deep help — fouls and blow-bys
Forgetting that pack line still requires boxing out — it is not a zone
description: Pack line defense: sag inside an imaginary line, protect the paint, and force contested jumpers — the system that stops drives.
gameSituations: Against drive-heavy teams that live in the paint
When your roster is less athletic but disciplined
To protect a lead — it bleeds the clock and forces jumpers
As a base defense for youth teams learning help principles

howTo.detail: Imagine a line about two meters inside the three-point arc — the 'pack line.' Off-ball defenders never go outside it. This packs five defenders into the scoring area.
howTo.title: Establish the pack line

howTo.detail: The on-ball defender pressures the ball hard — no easy passes, no comfortable dribbles. The pack behind him allows aggressive ball pressure because help is always near.
howTo.title: Pressure the ball handler

howTo.detail: Every off-ball defender plays one big gap inside the pack line, seeing both ball and man. The paint is always crowded; driving lanes do not exist.
howTo.title: Play big gaps inside the line

howTo.detail: When the ball is passed out, defenders close out from the pack — under control, high hands — then recover back inside the line on the next pass.
howTo.title: Close out, then sink back

howTo.detail: Because the defense concedes perimeter shots, it must dominate the glass. Every defender boxes out; the pack gives inside position to start.
howTo.title: Finish possessions with rebounds

title: Pack Line Defense
whatIsIt: Pack line defense is a sagging man-to-man system built on one rule: off-ball defenders stay inside an imaginary 'pack line' about two meters inside the three-point arc. Everyone packs into the paint area, daring the offense to beat them with jump shots.

It is man-to-man with training wheels for help: because everyone starts inside, help is always close, driving lanes never open, and the defense always has numbers at the rim. The trade-off is obvious — it concedes three-point attempts — but it concedes them as contested, rhythm-breaking shots after the offense has been frustrated inside.
whyItMatters: Most amateur and youth offenses cannot win shooting contested jumpers all game — they win on layups and open threes created by drives. Pack line takes away exactly those shots. It is also the best teaching system in basketball: it forces players to learn gaps, help, closeouts, and communication in their simplest form.
